claims.claim: Legend says the Devil wrote the book
claims.quote: The codex's extraordinary length, size, and detail have given rise to the legend that it was written by one scribe in one night with help from the Devil himself.

claims.claim: The Devil portrait is on folio 290
claims.quote: Folio 290 recto, otherwise empty, includes a full-page portrait of Satan, the Devil, about 50 cm (20 in) tall.

claims.claim: The Devil is about 50 cm tall and the page is otherwise empty
claims.quote: Folio 290 recto, otherwise empty, includes a full-page portrait of Satan, the Devil, about 50 cm (20 in) tall.

claims.claim: The pages before the Devil illustration darkened because readers turned to look at it, exposing them to light
claims.quote: The discoloration is because these vellum pages have been exposed to the light as readers turned the pages toward the infamous illustration over the centuries.

claims.claim: The codex is 92 cm long
claims.quote: At 92 cm (36 in) long, 50 cm (20 in) wide and 22 cm (8.7 in) thick, it is the largest known medieval manuscript.

claims.claim: The codex weighs 74.8 kg
claims.quote: Weighing 74.8 kg (165 lb), Codex Gigas is composed of 310 leaves of vellum claimed to be made from the skins of 160 donkeys, or perhaps calfskin

claims.claim: It has 310 leaves of vellum, claimed to be from the skins of 160 donkeys
claims.quote: Codex Gigas is composed of 310 leaves of vellum claimed to be made from the skins of 160 donkeys, or perhaps calfskin

claims.claim: Fifty-seven illuminated capitals survive
claims.quote: Capital letters at the start of books of the bible and the chronicle are elaborately illuminated in several colours, sometimes taking up most of the page; 57 of these survive.

claims.claim: The manuscript is written in Latin except for two Hebrew alphabets
claims.quote: The first page has two Hebrew alphabets. ... Apart from the alphabets at the start, the entire book is written in Latin.

claims.claim: The Hebrew alphabets are on the first page, next to the opening of Genesis
claims.quote: Sample tables of various alphabets on the first page of  Codex Gigas , including a Glagolitic and a Cyrillic sample (pasted in at a later date), next to the incipit of the Book of Genesis.

claims.claim: The book was thrown from a burning castle and hit a bystander
claims.quote: The Codex Gigas was saved by being thrown out of a window; according to the vicar Johann Erichsons, it landed on and injured a bystander.

claims.claim: Swedish troops took it as war booty in 1648
claims.quote: At the end of the Thirty Years' War in 1648, the entire collection was taken as war booty by the Swedish Army.

claims.claim: The Stockholm castle fire occurred in 1697
claims.quote: On 7 May 1697, a fire at the Tre Kronor royal castle in Stockholm destroyed much of the Swedish Royal Library.

claims.claim: The fire was at the Tre Kronor castle in Stockholm
claims.quote: On 7 May 1697, a fire at the Tre Kronor royal castle in Stockholm destroyed much of the Swedish Royal Library.

claims.claim: The vicar Johann Erichsons recorded that the book landed on and injured a bystander
claims.quote: according to the vicar Johann Erichsons, it landed on and injured a bystander

claims.claim: Glagolitic and Cyrillic alphabet slips were pasted in at a later date
claims.quote: including a Glagolitic and a Cyrillic sample (pasted in at a later date)

claims.claim: There are two small sheets of sample alphabets added to the first page beside the start of Genesis
claims.quote: There are also added slips with Early Cyrillic and Glagolitic alphabets (Folio 1).

claims.claim: Handwriting analysis indicates a single scribe wrote the book
claims.quote: It has been verified by extensive handwriting analysis that it was written by one monk

claims.claim: The book took an estimated 20 to 30 years to complete
claims.quote: it is estimated to have been completed over the span of 20-30 years

claims.claim: Twelve leaves were later removed, and it is unknown who removed them or why
claims.quote: It initially contained 320 sheets. However, twelve of these were subsequently removed. It is unknown who removed the pages or for what purpose.

claims.claim: The codex originally contained 320 leaves
claims.quote: It initially contained 320 sheets.

claims.claim: It is the largest surviving medieval manuscript in the world
claims.quote: The Codex Gigas ("Giant Book"; Czech: Obří kniha) is the largest extant medieval illuminated manuscript in the world, at a length of 92 cm (36 in).

claims.claim: It measures 50 cm wide and 22 cm thick
claims.quote: At 92 cm (36 in) long, 50 cm (20 in) wide and 22 cm (8.7 in) thick, it is the largest known medieval manuscript.

claims.claim: It was made in the early 13th century at the Benedictine monastery of Podlažice in Bohemia
claims.quote: The manuscript was created in the early 13th century in the Benedictine monastery of Podlažice in Chrast, Bohemia, now a region in the modern-day Czech Republic.

claims.claim: Contents include the complete Latin Vulgate Bible, Josephus, Isidore of Seville's Etymologiae, the chronicle of Cosmas of Prague, and medical treatises
claims.quote: Between the Old and New Testaments is a selection of other popular medieval reference works: Flavius Josephus's Antiquities of the Jews and The Jewish War, Isidore of Seville's encyclopedia Etymologiae, the chronicle of Cosmas of Prague (Chronica Boemorum), and medical works

claims.claim: The records in the codex stop in 1222
claims.quote: Records in the codex end in the year 1222.

claims.claim: The Devil has a dark green head, red horns and claws, four fingers on each hand, and two red tongues
claims.quote:
His hands and feet end with only four fingers and toes each, terminating in large claws; his claws and large horns are red.
He has a large, dark green head

claims.claim: Facing the Devil is a full-page depiction of the Kingdom of Heaven
claims.quote: Directly opposite the Devil is a full page depiction of the Kingdom of Heaven, thus juxtaposing contrasting images of Good and Evil as Christian symbols.

claims.claim: The legend tells of a monk sentenced to be walled up alive who promised to write in one night a book holding all human knowledge
claims.quote: the scribe was a Christian monk who broke his monastic vows and was sentenced to be walled up alive. To escape death, he promised to create, in one night, a book to glorify the monastery forever, including all human knowledge.

claims.claim: Near midnight the monk prayed to Lucifer for help
claims.quote: Near midnight, he became so desperate that he prayed to Lucifer to help him finish the book in exchange for his soul.

claims.claim: The manuscript is now at the National Library of Sweden
claims.quote: the manuscript is now preserved at the National Library of Sweden in Stockholm, where it is on display for the general public.
